# Chen Kai Blog

> Machine Learning, Mathematics, and Computer Science — explained for humans.
This file gives AI crawlers and assistants a machine-readable index of chenk.top, organized by series.

## Abstract Algebra

- [Abstract Algebra (1): Groups — Your First Encounter with Algebraic Structure](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/01-groups-first-encounter/): From integers to symmetries, we build the formal definition of a group, prove Lagrange's theorem, and compute our first subgroup lattice.
- [Abstract Algebra (2): Group Actions — How Groups Move Things Around](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/02-group-actions-and-symmetry/): We formalize how groups act on sets, prove the orbit-stabilizer theorem, derive Burnside's lemma, and count necklaces.
- [Abstract Algebra (3): Quotient Groups and Homomorphisms: The Art of Collapsing Structure](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/03-quotient-groups-and-homomorphisms/): Normal subgroups, quotient constructions, and the isomorphism theorems — how to systematically simplify groups while preserving their essence.
- [Abstract Algebra (4): Sylow Theorems — Dissecting Finite Groups](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/04-sylow-theorems/): The Sylow theorems give us a systematic way to find and count subgroups of prime-power order — the sharpest tool for classifying finite groups.
- [Abstract Algebra (5): Rings and Ideals — When Multiplication Enters the Picture](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/05-rings-and-ideals/): Adding multiplication to the mix: rings, integral domains, ideals, and quotient rings — the algebraic structures behind number theory and polynomial arithmetic.
- [Abstract Algebra (6): Polynomial Rings — Factorization and Unique Decomposition](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/06-polynomial-rings/): The division algorithm, irreducibility tests, and the climb from Z to Z[x] to Q[x] — understanding when and why unique factorization holds.
- [Abstract Algebra (7): Field Extensions — Building Bigger Number Systems](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/07-field-extensions/): Algebraic and transcendental extensions, the tower law, minimal polynomials, and splitting fields — the machinery that makes Galois theory possible.
- [Abstract Algebra (8): Galois Theory — The Bridge Between Fields and Groups](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/08-galois-theory/): The Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory establishes a perfect correspondence between intermediate fields and subgroups — and settles the ancient question of solvability by radicals.
- [Abstract Algebra (9): Modules — Generalizing Vector Spaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/09-modules/): Modules over rings generalize vector spaces over fields — the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over PIDs unifies the theory of abelian groups and canonical forms.
- [Abstract Algebra (10): Representation Theory — Groups Acting on Vector Spaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/10-representation-theory/): Representing abstract groups as matrices makes them concrete and computable — Maschke's theorem, Schur's lemma, and character theory give us powerful classification tools.
- [Abstract Algebra (11): Category Theory — The Language of Mathematical Structure](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/11-category-theory/): Categories, functors, and natural transformations provide a universal language for mathematical structure — and universal properties replace ad hoc constructions with elegant characterizations.
- [Abstract Algebra (12): Algebra in the Wild — Cryptography, Coding Theory, and Beyond](https://www.chenk.top/en/abstract-algebra/12-applications/): From RSA encryption to error-correcting codes to particle physics — abstract algebra's most powerful real-world applications, and where to go next.

## Aliyun Bailian

- [Aliyun Bailian (1): Platform Overview and First Request](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/01-platform-overview/): A practitioner's tour of Alibaba Cloud Bailian (DashScope) — what's actually in the model catalog, the two endpoint flavors, the async task pattern, and a working sample request to ground the rest of the series.
- [Aliyun Bailian (2): The Qwen LLM API in Production](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/02-qwen-llm-api/): Picking a Qwen variant by latency and cost, function calling done right, JSON mode without tears, and the enable_thinking + streaming requirement that the docs gloss over.
- [Aliyun Bailian (3): Qwen-Omni for Video, Audio, and Image Understanding](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/03-qwen-omni-multimodal/): Qwen-Omni for production multimodal: the four input types, the streaming requirement that the docs do not warn you about, and a working video-understanding pipeline with sane pixel budgets.
- [Aliyun Bailian (4): Wanxiang Video Generation End-to-End](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/04-wanxiang-video-generation/): Wanxiang text-to-video and image-to-video for production: the async task pattern, polling with backoff, prompt techniques that survive contact with reality, and the OSS write-through that saves you when result URLs expire.
- [Aliyun Bailian (5): Qwen-TTS for Multilingual Voice](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/05-qwen-tts-voice/): Qwen-TTS-Flash for production: native-only API, the 40+ voice catalog (including Cantonese and Sichuanese), streaming synthesis, and the SSML quirks that the docs gloss over.
- [Aliyun Bailian (6): Qwen3-Coder and Coding Agents](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/06-qwen-coder-agents/): Calling Qwen3-Coder-Plus on Model Studio, driving the qwen-code CLI, and wiring it into Claude Code with three env vars.
- [Aliyun Bailian (7): Built-in Web Search and Code Interpreter](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-bailian/07-builtin-tools/): Server-side web_search, web_extractor, and code_interpreter through the Responses API — a mini-agent without writing the tool loop.

## Alibaba Cloud Full Stack

- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (1): The Ecosystem Map — What Alibaba Cloud Actually Is](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/01-ecosystem-map/): A no-BS guide to Alibaba Cloud's product ecosystem. We map every major service to its AWS/Azure/GCP equivalent, set up an account from scratch, and deploy our first ECS instance — all in under an hour.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (2): ECS — Compute That Actually Makes Sense](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/02-ecs-compute/): Everything you need to know about ECS: instance families (g8, c8, r8, GPU), pricing models, cloud-init automation, security groups, and key pairs. We deploy a production-ready app server from scratch.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (3): VPC, SLB, and the Network Layer](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/03-vpc-networking/): Build a production network from scratch: VPC architecture, CIDR planning, VSwitches across availability zones, security groups as stateful firewalls, SLB for load balancing, NAT Gateway for outbound traffic, and EIP for public access.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (4): OSS — Object Storage Done Right](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/04-oss-storage/): Master Alibaba Cloud OSS: bucket types, storage classes, access control (ACL, RAM, STS, signed URLs), lifecycle rules, cross-region replication, CDN integration, and custom domains. Build a complete media storage backend.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (5): RDS and PolarDB — The Database Layer](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/05-rds-database/): RDS MySQL vs PolarDB: when to use which. Instance sizing, read replicas, proxy endpoints, backup/restore, monitoring, slow query analysis. Build a production database with HA and read scaling.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (6): RAM, KMS, and Cloud Security](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/06-ram-security/): Lock down your cloud: RAM users, groups, roles, and policies. STS for temporary credentials. KMS for encryption. ActionTrail for audit logging. Build a secure multi-team access model with least privilege.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (7): SLS, CloudMonitor, and Observability](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/07-observability/): Build full-stack observability: SLS for log collection and querying, CloudMonitor for metrics and alerts, ARMS for distributed tracing. Set up a complete monitoring stack for a production web application.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (8): Serverless — Function Compute and EventBridge](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/08-serverless/): Go serverless on Alibaba Cloud: Function Compute triggers, runtimes, cold starts, and pricing. EventBridge for event routing. API Gateway integration. Build an event-driven image processing pipeline.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (9): OpenSearch and AI Search](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/09-opensearch/): From keyword search to AI-powered retrieval: OpenSearch service, vector search for RAG, LLM-powered query rewriting, and hybrid search. Build a product search engine combining vectors and keywords.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (10): Bailian and DashScope — The LLM Layer](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/10-bailian-llm/): The complete LLM toolkit on Alibaba Cloud: Qwen model family, DashScope API (OpenAI-compatible), Wanxiang image/video generation, Qwen TTS, async task patterns, and fine-tuning. Build a multi-modal AI pipeline.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (11): PAI — The ML Platform](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/11-pai-ml-platform/): The complete ML platform on Alibaba Cloud: PAI-DSW for notebooks, PAI-DLC for distributed training, PAI-EAS for model serving, Designer for visual workflows, and Model Gallery. Train and deploy a custom model end-to-end.
- [Alibaba Cloud Full Stack (12): End-to-End — One Terraform Apply for Everything](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-fullstack/12-terraform-e2e/): The grand finale: codify everything from Parts 1-11 into Terraform modules. VPC, ECS, RDS, OSS, RAM, SLS, Function Compute — all provisioned with one terraform apply. Plus CI/CD with GitHub Actions and cost optimization.

## Aliyun PAI

- [Aliyun PAI (1): Platform Overview and the Product Family Map](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-pai/01-platform-overview/): What Aliyun PAI actually is in 2026, the four-layer architecture from the official docs, the five sub-products you'll touch, and a sane account/workspace setup so the rest of the series can skip the boilerplate.
- [Aliyun PAI (2): PAI-DSW — Notebooks That Don't Eat Your Weights](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-pai/02-pai-dsw-notebook/): Working with PAI-DSW for real: choosing the right GPU image, mounting OSS so you don't lose checkpoints when the instance restarts, and an MNIST notebook drawn from the official Quick Start that you can copy-paste.
- [Aliyun PAI (3): PAI-DLC — Distributed Training Without the Cluster Pain](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-pai/03-pai-dlc-distributed-training/): Submit a real multi-GPU training job on PAI-DLC, understand the resource pools (Lingjun vs general vs preemptible), and use AIMaster + EasyCKPT so a flaky node doesn't cost you a day.
- [Aliyun PAI (4): PAI-EAS — Model Serving, Cold Starts, and the TPS Lie](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-pai/04-pai-eas-model-serving/): End-to-end PAI-EAS for production: image-based deploy from OSS-mounted weights, the three inference modes, an autoscaler that doesn't blow your budget, and canary releases via service groups. Includes a working vLLM Qwen3 deployment from the official Quick Start.
- [Aliyun PAI (5): Designer vs Model Gallery — When the GUIs Actually Earn Their Keep](https://www.chenk.top/en/aliyun-pai/05-pai-designer-vs-quickstart/): PAI-Designer for tabular ML pipelines, Model Gallery for one-click open-source model deploy/fine-tune. The honest decision matrix for when to skip the SDK and let the GUI ship for you.

## Claude Code Hands-On

- [Claude Code Hands-On (1): Install, the Three-Layer Config, and the # @ /init Trio](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/01-install-and-config/): Install Claude Code, understand the three-layer settings.json system, and learn the three quietly powerful primitives: # to write into context, @ to reference files, /init to generate the project memory file.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (2): Shortcuts, the Four-State Toggle, and Thinking Modes](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/02-shortcuts-and-modes/): Shift+Tab is a four-state cycle, not a binary. Thinking modes have five levels. Escape and double-Escape do different things. Five shortcuts that reshape how Claude Code feels day-to-day.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (3): Custom Slash Commands and Conversation Control](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/03-custom-commands/): Slash commands turn repeated workflows into one-line invocations. $ARGUMENTS makes them parameterized. The right ones become your team's shared vocabulary.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (4): MCP Servers, or How Claude Talks to Anything](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/04-mcp-servers/): MCP is the plug-in protocol that lets Claude Code reach beyond your filesystem. Install one (Playwright), see it work end-to-end, and learn the permission model that keeps it from going feral.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (5): Hooks, or How to Stop Worrying About Yolo Mode](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/05-hooks/): Hooks are the shell scripts that run before and after every tool call. PreToolUse can block. PostToolUse can format, lint, log. Five hooks I use on every repo, and the one anti-pattern that bites everyone.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (6): The SDK, GitHub Integration, and Claude in CI](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/06-sdk-and-github/): The SDK turns Claude Code from a CLI into a library. GitHub Action makes it answer @claude on PRs. Together they let you put Claude inside the same CI pipeline that already runs your tests — without giving up control.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (7): Ten Hooks I Actually Use, with the Code](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/07-hooks-deep-dive/): Picking ten hooks out of the 100 in the reference repo and walking through each: what it does, the actual JS, the settings.json wire-up, and where it bites. PreToolUse for safety, PostToolUse for hygiene, the boring ones that earn their keep.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (8): Sub-Agents, Worktrees, and Plan Mode](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/08-subagents-worktrees-plan/): Three features that change what Claude Code can take on at once: sub-agents for parallel research, worktrees for isolation, plan mode for the moments before you let it touch anything. The boundaries between them, and when each is the wrong answer.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (9): settings.json, the Three-Layer Permission Model, and Env](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/09-settings-and-permissions/): settings.json is the file that decides what Claude can do, where, and with whose credentials. The three layers (user, project, local), the permission grammar, env vars that change behavior, and the precedence order that catches everyone the first time.
- [Claude Code Hands-On (10): Skills, and When to Reach for Each Extension Mechanism](https://www.chenk.top/en/claude-code-learn/10-skills-decision-tree/): Skills are the newest extension mechanism in Claude Code: a folder, a SKILL.md, and a body of instructions the model loads on demand. How they differ from slash commands, MCP servers, and hooks — with a decision tree for which one to reach for.

## Cloud Computing

- [Cloud Computing (1): Fundamentals and Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/fundamentals/): An engineering-grade introduction to cloud computing -- service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, FaaS), deployment topologies, the economics of CapEx vs OpEx, regions and AZs, vendor catalogues and a decision framework with real architecture cases.
- [Cloud Computing (2): Virtualization Technology Deep Dive](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/virtualization/): A hands-on guide to virtualization -- hypervisors (VMware, KVM, Xen, Hyper-V), storage and network virtualization, performance tuning, and container comparison.
- [Cloud Computing (3): Cloud-Native and Container Technologies](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/cloud-native-containers/): Why cloud-native exists, what containers actually do at the kernel level, how Kubernetes really works, when service mesh is worth its weight, and how the whole stack fits together in production.
- [Cloud Computing (4): Cloud Storage Systems and Distributed Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/storage-systems/): From CAP theorem to S3, HDFS, and Ceph -- a deep tour of distributed storage primitives, consistency, replication, erasure coding, and cost optimisation.
- [Cloud Computing (5): Cloud Network Architecture and SDN](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/networking-sdn/): VPC, load balancers, CDN, SDN/NFV, and BGP -- a deep tour of cloud networking from packet to planet, with the production knobs that matter.
- [Cloud Computing (6): Cloud Security and Privacy Protection](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/security-privacy/): A working engineer's guide to cloud security: shared responsibility, IAM that actually scales, encryption at rest / in transit / in use, zero trust, compliance frameworks, and incident response that you can rehearse.
- [Cloud Computing (7): Cloud Operations and DevOps Practices](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/operations-devops/): A working DevOps engineer's guide: CI/CD pipelines that gate quality, Terraform for reproducible infrastructure, Prometheus + Grafana monitoring, ELK/EFK logging, SRE error budgets, and the operational habits that keep services up at 3 AM.
- [Cloud Computing (8): Multi-Cloud and Hybrid Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/cloud-computing/multi-cloud-hybrid/): Series finale. Multi-cloud vs hybrid cloud strategy, the 6R migration framework, hybrid networking, cross-cloud data sync and conflict resolution, vendor lock-in mitigation, disaster recovery RPO/RTO planning, FinOps cost optimization, and the trends shaping the next decade.

## Computer Fundamentals

- [Computer Fundamentals (1): CPU and the Computing Core](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/01-cpu/): Understand data units (bits and bytes), CPU architecture, the 5-stage pipeline, cache hierarchy, branch prediction, out-of-order execution, multi-core and SMT, Intel vs AMD differences, and how to choose the right processor.
- [Computer Fundamentals (2): Memory and Cache Systems](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/02-memory/): How memory really works: hierarchy, DRAM vs SRAM, virtual memory, the TLB, ECC, NUMA, and channel scaling — explained from circuits to system design.
- [Computer Fundamentals (3): Storage Systems (HDD vs SSD)](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/03-storage/): Compare HDD and SSD working principles, SATA vs NVMe interface speeds, SLC/MLC/TLC/QLC lifespan, SSD optimization (4K alignment, TRIM), and RAID array configurations.
- [Computer Fundamentals (4): Motherboard, Graphics, and Expansion](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/04-motherboard-gpu/): Read a motherboard floor plan, understand PCIe lane allocation across CPU and chipset, follow the SIMT execution model that makes GPUs fast, compare DDR/GDDR/HBM memory, and pick the right display interface.
- [Computer Fundamentals (5): Network, Power, and Troubleshooting](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/05-network-power/): Deep dive into the NIC pipeline (PHY/MAC/DMA), TCP handshake, network topologies, PSU efficiency curves, datacenter PUE, component power hierarchy, and UPS architecture.
- [Computer Fundamentals (6): Deep Dive and System Integration](https://www.chenk.top/en/computer-fundamentals/06-deep-dive/): Series finale. We zoom out from individual components to the whole system: how CPU, cache, memory, storage, IO, and accelerators are wired together; how hardware-aware software wins by 100×; how to read performance counters; and where computing is heading next — chiplets, photonics, and quantum.

## Databases

- [Databases (1): Data Models and SQL — Why Tables Won (For Now)](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/01-data-models-and-sql/): A ground-up tour of the relational model, SQL fundamentals, normalization, and advanced query patterns — everything you need to speak fluent SQL.
- [Databases (2): Indexing and Query Planning — How Databases Find Your Data](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/02-indexing-and-query-planning/): Deep dive into B-tree and B+tree indexes, hash indexes, composite indexes, covering indexes, and how to read EXPLAIN output to diagnose slow queries.
- [Databases (3): Transactions and Concurrency — ACID, Isolation Levels, and Locking](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/03-transactions-and-concurrency/): A thorough guide to ACID properties, isolation levels, MVCC, locking strategies, and deadlock prevention — with concrete SQL examples for every concept.
- [Databases (4): Storage Engines — How Data Hits Disk](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/04-storage-engines/): How database storage engines work under the hood — B-tree vs LSM-tree, WAL, buffer pools, compaction, and why your choice of engine shapes everything.
- [Databases (5): NoSQL — Document, Key-Value, Column, and Graph](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/05-nosql-landscape/): A practical tour of the four major NoSQL families — document, key-value, wide-column, and graph — including the CAP theorem and when to use each model.
- [Databases (6): Replication and Partitioning — Scaling Beyond One Machine](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/06-replication-and-partitioning/): How databases replicate data for availability and partition data for scale — covering leader-follower, multi-leader, leaderless, sharding strategies, and consistent hashing.
- [Databases (7): Distributed Transactions — 2PC, Saga, and Why Consensus Is Hard](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/07-distributed-transactions/): How distributed databases coordinate transactions across machines — two-phase commit, Raft consensus, the Saga pattern, and practical patterns like outbox and CDC.
- [Databases (8): Databases in Practice — Migration, Monitoring, and War Stories](https://www.chenk.top/en/databases/08-database-in-practice/): The operational side of databases — schema migrations, connection pooling, monitoring, backup strategies, managed database options, and hard-won lessons from production incidents.

## Differential Geometry

- [Differential Geometry (1): Curves in Space — Curvature, Torsion, and the Frenet Frame](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/01-curves-in-space/): Parametrized curves, arc length, curvature, torsion, and the Frenet-Serret apparatus — the complete local theory of space curves.
- [Differential Geometry (2): Surfaces and the First Fundamental Form: Intrinsic Measurements](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/02-surfaces-first-form/): Regular surfaces, coordinate patches, the tangent plane, and the first fundamental form — how to measure lengths, angles, and areas on a surface without leaving it.
- [Differential Geometry (3): The Shape Operator — Curvature of Surfaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/03-second-form-curvature/): The Gauss map and shape operator capture how a surface bends in space — principal, Gaussian, and mean curvatures classify every point as elliptic, hyperbolic, or parabolic.
- [Differential Geometry (4): Intrinsic Geometry — Theorema Egregium and Geodesics](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/04-intrinsic-geometry/): Gauss's Theorema Egregium reveals that Gaussian curvature depends only on the first form — geodesics are the 'straight lines' of curved surfaces, minimizing arc length locally.
- [Differential Geometry (5): The Gauss-Bonnet Theorem — Where Geometry Meets Topology](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/05-gauss-bonnet/): The Gauss-Bonnet theorem connects total Gaussian curvature to the Euler characteristic — a stunning bridge between local differential geometry and global topology.
- [Differential Geometry (6): Smooth Manifolds — Geometry Beyond Embedded Surfaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/06-smooth-manifolds/): Manifolds free geometry from ambient space — charts, atlases, and smooth structure let us do calculus on spaces that don't live in R^n.
- [Differential Geometry (7): Vector Fields, Flows, and the Lie Bracket](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/07-vector-fields-flows/): Vector fields generate flows — one-parameter families of diffeomorphisms. The Lie bracket measures the failure of flows to commute, leading to Frobenius integrability.
- [Differential Geometry (8): Differential Forms — The Natural Language of Integration on Manifolds](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/08-differential-forms/): Differential forms unify gradient, curl, and divergence into a single framework — the exterior derivative d and wedge product turn calculus coordinate-free.
- [Differential Geometry (9): Integration on Manifolds and Stokes' Theorem](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/09-integration-stokes/): Stokes' theorem — the fundamental theorem of calculus on manifolds — unifies Green's, Gauss's, and the classical Stokes' theorems into one elegant statement.
- [Differential Geometry (10): Riemannian Geometry — Metrics, Connections, and Parallel Transport](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/10-riemannian-geometry/): A Riemannian metric lets us measure lengths, angles, and volumes on any smooth manifold — the Levi-Civita connection provides the canonical notion of parallel transport and geodesics.
- [Differential Geometry (11): Curvature in Riemannian Geometry — Riemann, Ricci, and Scalar](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/11-curvature-on-manifolds/): The Riemann curvature tensor captures all intrinsic curvature information — its contractions (Ricci and scalar curvature) control volume growth, geodesic deviation, and Einstein's equations.
- [Differential Geometry (12): Fiber Bundles, Characteristic Classes, and Physics](https://www.chenk.top/en/differential-geometry/12-bundles-and-physics/): Vector bundles generalize the tangent bundle, connections on bundles generalize Levi-Civita, and characteristic classes are topological invariants — this is the geometry underlying gauge theory and general relativity.

## Docker and Containers

- [Docker and Containers (1): Why Containers — The Problem VMs Didn't Solve](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/01-why-containers/): Containers solve the 'works on my machine' problem that VMs made expensive. Learn what containers actually are, how they differ from VMs, and run your first one.
- [Docker and Containers (2): Images and Layers — What docker pull Actually Downloads](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/02-images-and-layers/): Docker images aren't monolithic files — they're stacks of read-only layers shared between containers. Understanding layers is the key to fast builds and small images.
- [Docker and Containers (3): Dockerfile Patterns — From Naive to Production](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/03-dockerfile-patterns/): A Dockerfile defines how your image is built. The difference between a naive Dockerfile and an optimized one can be 10x in image size and build time.
- [Docker and Containers (4): Networking and Volumes — How Containers Talk and Persist](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/04-networking-and-volumes/): Containers are ephemeral by default — they lose data when deleted and run in isolated networks. Volumes and networks are the two mechanisms that connect containers to the persistent, communicating world.
- [Docker and Containers (5): Docker Compose — Multi-Container Applications](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/05-docker-compose/): Real applications aren't single containers. Docker Compose lets you define multi-service architectures in a single YAML file — networks, volumes, dependencies, and all.
- [Docker and Containers (6): Debugging and Logging — When Things Go Wrong Inside a Box](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/06-debugging-and-logging/): Containers hide their internals by design. When something breaks, you need specific tools and techniques to see inside the box without breaking the isolation that makes containers useful.
- [Docker and Containers (7): Security — Running Containers Without Giving Away the Keys](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/07-security-and-best-practices/): Containers provide isolation, not security. Default Docker configurations run processes as root with full capabilities. This article shows how to lock containers down for production.
- [Docker and Containers (8): Beyond Docker — Kubernetes, Swarm, and What Comes Next](https://www.chenk.top/en/docker-containers/08-orchestration-preview/): Single-host Docker breaks down at scale. This article previews container orchestration — Docker Swarm for simplicity, Kubernetes for everything else — and maps out the broader cloud-native ecosystem.

## Functional Analysis

- [Functional Analysis (1): Metric Spaces — Distance, Convergence, and Completeness](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/01-metric-spaces/): From the real line to infinite-dimensional function spaces: why completeness is the dividing line.
- [Functional Analysis (2): Normed Spaces and Banach Spaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/02-normed-and-banach/): Norm axioms, classical examples, equivalence of norms in finite dimensions, completeness and why it matters, Schauder bases, quotient spaces, and the role of separability.
- [Functional Analysis (3): Hilbert Spaces — Geometry in Infinite Dimensions](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/03-hilbert-spaces/): Inner products give infinite-dimensional spaces geometric structure — orthogonality, projections, and the Riesz representation theorem make Hilbert spaces the analyst's paradise.
- [Functional Analysis (4): Dual Spaces and the Hahn-Banach Theorem — Taming Linear Functionals](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/04-dual-spaces-hahn-banach/): The Hahn-Banach theorem guarantees enough continuous linear functionals exist to separate points — the foundation for duality theory in functional analysis.
- [Functional Analysis (5): Weak and Weak-* Topologies — When Norm Convergence Is Too Strong](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/05-weak-topologies/): Norm topology is too fine for many purposes — weak and weak-* topologies provide the compactness results that make optimization and PDE theory work.
- [Functional Analysis (6): Bounded Linear Operators and the Big Theorems](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/06-bounded-operators/): The Uniform Boundedness Principle, Open Mapping Theorem, and Closed Graph Theorem — three consequences of completeness that constrain how operators can behave.
- [Functional Analysis (7): Compact Operators — The Bridge to Finite Dimensions](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/07-compact-operators/): Compact operators are limits of finite-rank operators and inherit much finite-dimensional spectral behavior — the Fredholm alternative and spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators.
- [Functional Analysis (8): Spectral Theory — Decomposing Operators](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/08-spectral-theory/): The spectrum generalizes eigenvalues to infinite dimensions — the spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators and continuous functional calculus give us a complete decomposition.
- [Functional Analysis (9): Unbounded Operators — When Boundedness Fails](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/09-unbounded-operators/): Closed operators, the distinction between symmetric and self-adjoint, deficiency indices, Friedrichs extension, the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators, and Stone's theorem.
- [Functional Analysis (10): Semigroups of Operators — Evolution Equations in Infinite Dimensions](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/10-semigroups/): C₀-semigroups provide the abstract framework for evolution equations — the Hille-Yosida theorem characterizes which operators generate well-posed dynamics.
- [Functional Analysis (11): Distributions and Sobolev Spaces — Generalized Solutions](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/11-distributions-sobolev/): Distributions extend the notion of function to handle derivatives that don't exist classically — Sobolev spaces provide the right setting for weak solutions to PDE.
- [Functional Analysis (12): Functional Analysis in Action — PDE and Quantum Mechanics](https://www.chenk.top/en/functional-analysis/12-applications-pde-qm/): Lax-Milgram for elliptic PDE, variational methods, quantum observables as self-adjoint operators, and Stone's theorem — where the abstract theory meets concrete applications.

## Kernel Methods

- [Kernel Methods (1): Why We Need Them — Hitting the Ceiling of Linear Algorithms](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/01-why-kernels/): Linear algorithms can't capture non-linear patterns. The kernel trick lets you keep the linear algorithm's elegance AND model non-linear relationships — without writing the high-dimensional feature map. Part 1 of an 8-part series.
- [Kernel Methods (2): Mathematical Foundations — Positive-Definite Kernels and Mercer's Theorem](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/02-kernel-math-foundations/): What makes a function a valid kernel? Positive-definiteness, the Gram matrix test, and Mercer's theorem — the spectral decomposition that justifies the kernel trick.
- [Kernel Methods (3): RKHS — The Theoretical Soul of Kernel Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/03-rkhs/): Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space — the function space where kernel methods live. The reproducing property, the representer theorem, and why finite-data optimization works in infinite dimensions.
- [Kernel Methods (4): Common Kernel Families — RBF, Matern, Polynomial, Periodic, and More](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/04-common-kernels/): A tour of the kernels you'll actually use: RBF (Gaussian), polynomial, linear, Matern, periodic, sigmoid. When to pick which, hyperparameter intuition, and how kernels combine.
- [Kernel Methods (5): Kernel SVM, Kernel PCA, and Kernel Ridge Regression](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/05-kernel-algorithms/): The classic algorithms, kernelized — SVM's dual form, Kernel PCA's eigendecomposition in feature space, and Kernel Ridge's closed-form solution. With sklearn code and worked examples.
- [Kernel Methods (6): Gaussian Processes — When Kernels Meet Bayesian Inference](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/06-gaussian-processes/): Gaussian Processes turn kernels into a Bayesian model — posterior with uncertainty, marginal likelihood for hyperparameters, and the kernel as a prior over functions.
- [Kernel Methods (7): Large-Scale Kernels — Nystrom Approximation and Random Fourier Features](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/07-large-scale-kernels/): Kernel methods are O(n^3). Nystrom approximation and Random Fourier Features pull them back to linear time without giving up the kernel trick's expressive power.
- [Kernel Methods (8): Deep Kernel Learning vs Deep Learning — A Practitioner's Guide](https://www.chenk.top/en/kernel-methods/08-deep-kernels-vs-dl/): Deep kernel learning combines neural feature extractors with kernel methods. When to pick kernels over deep nets, hyperparameter tuning playbook, common failure modes, and a final 5-step kernel decision flowchart.

## LeetCode Patterns

- [LeetCode (1): Patterns — Hash Tables](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/hash-tables/): Master hash table patterns through four classic LeetCode problems — Two Sum, Group Anagrams, Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters, and Top K Frequent Elements. Learn complement search, canonical-form grouping, sliding window with counts, and bucket sort by frequency.
- [LeetCode (2): Patterns — Two Pointers](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/two-pointers/): A deep tour of the two-pointer family: collision, fast/slow, sliding window, and partition pointers. Five problems (Two Sum II, 3Sum, Container With Most Water, Linked List Cycle, Move Zeroes) explained with invariants, complexity proofs, and a decision tree.
- [LeetCode (3): Patterns — Linked List Operations](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/linked-list-operations/): A complete linked list toolkit: reversal (iterative and recursive), merging sorted lists, Floyd's cycle detection, removing the nth node from end, and an LRU cache built on a doubly linked list plus hash map.
- [LeetCode (4): Patterns — Sliding Window Technique](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/sliding-window/): Master fixed-size and variable-size sliding window patterns. Solve Maximum Sum Subarray, Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters, Minimum Window Substring, and Permutation in String.
- [LeetCode (5): Patterns — Binary Search](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/binary-search/): A working coder's guide to binary search: three templates, rotated arrays, peak finding, and binary search on the answer with worked traces and figures.
- [LeetCode (6): Patterns — Binary Tree Traversal and Construction](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/binary-tree-traversal/): A unified mental model for binary trees: how the four traversal orders are really one DFS recipe, why recursion and an explicit stack are the same algorithm, and how to reconstruct a tree from preorder + inorder. Includes Inorder Traversal, Level Order Traversal, Construct from Preorder + Inorder, Maximum Depth, and Validate BST.
- [LeetCode (7): Patterns — Dynamic Programming Basics](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/dynamic-programming-basics/): Master dynamic programming through a single recipe: define the state, write the transition, anchor the base case. Worked solutions for Climbing Stairs, House Robber, Coin Change, LIS, 0/1 Knapsack, LCS, and Edit Distance.
- [LeetCode (8): Patterns — Backtracking Algorithms](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/backtracking/): Master the universal backtracking template through six classic problems: Permutations, Combinations, Subsets, Word Search, N-Queens, and Sudoku Solver. Learn the choose -> recurse -> un-choose pattern and the pruning techniques that make it fast.
- [LeetCode (9): Patterns — Greedy Algorithms](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/09-greedy-algorithms/): When does picking the locally best option give the global optimum? A working tour of greedy algorithms with proofs (exchange argument), classic problems (Jump Game, Gas Station, Interval Scheduling, Task Scheduler, Partition Labels), and a clear rule for when greedy fails.
- [LeetCode (10): Patterns — Stack and Queue](https://www.chenk.top/en/leetcode/stack-and-queue/): Master stack and queue applications: valid parentheses, monotonic stack for next greater element, BFS with queues, priority queues for top-K problems, and deque for sliding window maximum.

## Linear Algebra

- [Essence of Linear Algebra (1): The Essence of Vectors — More Than Just Arrows](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/01-the-essence-of-vectors/): Vectors are everywhere -- from GPS navigation to Netflix recommendations. This chapter builds your intuition from arrows in space to abstract vector spaces, covering addition, scalar multiplication, inner products, norms, and why linearity matters.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (2): Linear Combinations and Vector Spaces](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/02-linear-combinations-and-vector-spaces/): If vectors are building blocks, linear combinations are the blueprint. This chapter develops the five concepts that the rest of linear algebra is built on: span, linear independence, basis, dimension, and subspaces.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (3): Matrices as Linear Transformations](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/03-matrices-as-linear-transformations/): Matrices are not tables of numbers -- they are machines that transform space. This chapter shows you how to see rotation, scaling, shearing, reflection, and projection as matrices, and why matrix multiplication means composing transformations.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (4): The Secrets of Determinants](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/04-the-secrets-of-determinants/): Determinants are not just tedious calculations -- they measure how much a transformation stretches or compresses space. This chapter gives you the geometric intuition behind determinants, their key properties, and practical applications.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (5): Linear Systems and Column Space](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/05-linear-systems-and-column-space/): When does Ax = b have a solution? How many? The honest answer is geometric: it depends on whether b lives inside the column space of A, and on how much of the input space A crushes to zero. This chapter weaves Gaussian elimination, column space, null space, rank, and the rank-nullity theorem into one structural picture.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (6): Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/06-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/): Some special vectors survive a matrix transformation with their direction intact -- they only get scaled. These eigenvectors and their eigenvalues reveal the deepest structure of linear transformations, powering everything from Google search to PCA.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (7): Orthogonality and Projections — When Vectors Mind Their Own Business](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/07-orthogonality-and-projections/): Orthogonality is what makes GPS work, noise-canceling headphones cancel, and JPEG compress. This chapter builds geometric intuition for orthogonal vectors, projections, Gram-Schmidt, QR decomposition, and least squares -- the backbone of modern scientific computing.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (8): Symmetric Matrices and Quadratic Forms — The Best Matrices in Town](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/08-symmetric-matrices-and-quadratic-forms/): Symmetric matrices are the 'nicest' matrices in linear algebra: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors, and perfect diagonalization. This chapter builds intuition for quadratic forms, positive definiteness, and why symmetric matrices dominate physics, optimization, and data science.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (9): Singular Value Decomposition — The Crown Jewel of Linear Algebra](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/09-singular-value-decomposition/): SVD decomposes any matrix -- not just square or symmetric ones. From image compression to Netflix recommendations, from face recognition to gene analysis, SVD is the most powerful and most universal decomposition in linear algebra.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (10): Matrix Norms and Condition Numbers — Is Your Linear System Healthy?](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/10-matrix-norms-and-condition-numbers/): The condition number is a 'health report' for a linear system — it tells you whether tiny input errors will explode into catastrophic output errors. This chapter covers vector norms, matrix norms, the spectral norm, condition numbers, and preconditioning.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (11): Matrix Calculus and Optimization — The Engine Behind Machine Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/11-matrix-calculus-and-optimization/): Adjusting the shower temperature is a tiny version of training a neural network: you change a parameter based on an error signal. Matrix calculus is the language that scales this idea to millions of parameters, and optimization is the engine that does the adjusting.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (12): Sparse Matrices and Compressed Sensing — Less Is More](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/12-sparse-matrices-and-compressed-sensing/): Sparsity is everywhere: JPEG photos, MRI scans, genomic data. Compressed sensing exploits this to recover signals from far fewer measurements than traditional theory requires. This chapter covers L1 regularization, LASSO, the RIP condition, and recovery algorithms.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (13): Tensors and Multilinear Algebra](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/13-tensors-and-multilinear-algebra/): From scalars to high-dimensional data cubes -- tensors generalize vectors and matrices to arbitrary dimensions. Learn CP and Tucker decomposition, see how tensors compress neural networks and power recommender systems, and build intuition with NumPy/TensorLy code.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (14): Random Matrix Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/14-random-matrix-theory/): Fill a huge matrix with random numbers, compute its eigenvalues, and watch stunning regularity emerge from chaos. Learn the Wigner semicircle law, Marchenko-Pastur distribution, and Tracy-Widom limit -- with applications to MIMO, finance, and PCA in ML.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (15): Linear Algebra in Machine Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/15-linear-algebra-in-machine-learning/): Machine learning speaks linear algebra as its native language. From PCA to SVMs, from matrix factorization in recommender systems to gradient descent optimization -- see how vectors, matrices, and decompositions power every core ML algorithm.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (16): Linear Algebra in Deep Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/16-linear-algebra-in-deep-learning/): Deep learning is large-scale matrix computation. From backpropagation as the chain rule in matrix form, to im2col turning convolutions into GEMM, to attention as soft retrieval via dot products -- see every core DL operation through the lens of linear algebra.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (17): Linear Algebra in Computer Vision](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/17-linear-algebra-in-computer-vision/): Images are matrices, geometric transformations are matrix multiplications, camera imaging is a projective map, and 3D reconstruction is solving linear systems. Master the linear algebra that quietly powers every corner of computer vision.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra (18): Frontiers and Summary](https://www.chenk.top/en/linear-algebra/18-frontiers-and-summary/): Series finale: quantum gates as unitary matrices, graph convolution as Laplacian filtering, attention as soft retrieval, LoRA as low-rank adaptation, tensor networks, the matrix exponential, free probability, and a topological data analysis preview -- plus the 18-chapter dependency graph and the geometry / numerics / computation triangle that runs through everything.

## Linux

- [Linux (1): Basics — Core Concepts and Essential Commands](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/basics/): Your entry guide to Linux: the multi-user permission model, the FHS directory tree, distribution lineages, and the command-line muscle memory you need before any deeper topic makes sense.
- [Linux (2): File Permissions — rwx, chmod, chown, and Beyond](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/file-permissions/): Master the Linux permission model: rwx semantics on files vs directories, numeric and symbolic notation, chmod/chown usage, umask defaults, SUID/SGID/Sticky bit, and ACLs.
- [Linux (3): Disk Management — Partitions, Filesystems, LVM, and the Mount Stack](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/disk-management/): End-to-end disk workflow on Linux: identify block devices with lsblk, partition with GPT, format with ext4 / xfs, mount persistently through /etc/fstab, expand capacity online with LVM, and debug the classic 'disk full but du can't find it' incidents.
- [Linux (4): Package Management — apt, dnf, pacman, and Building from Source](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/package-management/): Master package management across distributions: dpkg/apt for Debian/Ubuntu, rpm/yum/dnf for RHEL/CentOS, pacman for Arch, dependency troubleshooting, version locking, mirrors, and compiling from source.
- [Linux (5): User Management — Users, Groups, sudo, and Security](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/user-management/): A working mental model for Linux accounts: how /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow fit together, when to use a primary group versus a supplementary one, how sudo actually decides, and the full lifecycle of useradd / usermod / passwd / chage / userdel — including the PAM stack underneath.
- [Linux (6): Service Management — systemd, systemctl, and journald](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/service-management/): A working model of systemd: PID 1, units and targets, the service lifecycle, writing your own unit files, journalctl filtering, timers as a cron replacement, and a disciplined troubleshooting workflow.
- [Linux (7): Process and Resource Management: From `top` to cgroups](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/process-resource-management/): How processes are born and die on Linux: the fork/exec model, the state machine that ps and top print in the STAT column, the resource axes (CPU, memory, disk I/O, network) that actually constrain a server, the signals you should know by heart, and the cgroup + namespace primitives that turn all of this into containers.
- [Linux (8): Pipelines and File Operations — Composing Tools into Data Flows](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/pipelines/): A deep walk-through of the Unix pipeline model: stdin/stdout/stderr and file descriptors, every common redirection form, the grep/awk/sed/cut/sort/uniq/xargs toolchain, named pipes, and process substitution -- with one-liners you can actually use on logs.
- [Linux (9): Vim Essentials](https://www.chenk.top/en/linux/09-vim-essentials/): Learn Vim by understanding its grammar -- modes, operators + motions, text objects -- not by memorizing shortcuts. A practical, beginner-friendly guide with a one-week practice plan.

## LLM Engineering

- [LLM Engineering (1): Architectures from Transformer to MoE](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/01-architectures/): MHA → GQA → MQA, sparse MoE routing in Mixtral and Qwen3-MoE, sliding-window attention, and the state-space alternatives Mamba and RWKV — what each costs and where each wins.
- [LLM Engineering (2): Tokenization Deep Dive](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/02-tokenization/): BPE vs SentencePiece vs WordPiece, byte-level fallback, the CJK token-bloat problem, vocabulary expansion costs, and the chat-template tokens that silently shape every model's behavior.
- [LLM Engineering (3): Pretraining at Scale](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/03-pretraining/): Data mixing, deduplication, contamination, μP, FSDP vs ZeRO-3 vs pipeline parallel, the practical 200B-token cliff, and the failure modes that only appear above 1000 GPUs.
- [LLM Engineering (4): Post-training — SFT, DPO, RLHF, RLAIF](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/04-post-training/): What SFT, DPO, RLHF, and RLAIF each actually optimize, when reward models fail, KL constraints, the LoRA-vs-full-FT debate, and the production post-training recipes that ship in 2026.
- [LLM Engineering (5): Inference Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/05-inference/): KV cache mechanics, paged attention, continuous batching, speculative decoding, INT8/INT4/AWQ/GPTQ quantization, and the vLLM vs SGLang vs TensorRT-LLM tradeoffs.
- [LLM Engineering (6): Long Context — RoPE, YaRN, Sinks](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/06-long-context/): How RoPE encodes position, why naive extension breaks, NTK-aware and YaRN scaling, ALiBi vs RoPE, attention sinks for streaming, and why 1M-context claims often fail at retrieval.
- [LLM Engineering (7): Function Calling and Tool Use](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/07-function-calling/): JSON-mode vs function-mode vs free-form, parallel tool calls, structured-output guarantees with grammars, error recovery patterns, and the agent loops that survive contact with reality.
- [LLM Engineering (8): Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/08-rag/): Chunking strategies, dense vs sparse vs hybrid retrieval, reranker selection, the long-context-vs-RAG tradeoff in 2026, and the failure modes that show up at 100K+ documents.
- [LLM Engineering (9): Prompting at Production Scale](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/09-prompting/): Chain-of-thought when it actually helps, self-consistency, prompt-caching economics, jailbreak taxonomy, prompt-injection defenses, and the prompts that survive in production.
- [LLM Engineering (10): Evaluation](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/10-evaluation/): Why MMLU is broken, the contamination problem, LLM-as-judge biases, position-bias mitigation, calibration, and the A/B testing patterns that actually catch regressions in production.
- [LLM Engineering (11): Safety and Alignment](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/11-safety/): What alignment means engineering-wise, refusal calibration, the red-team taxonomy, hallucination metrics, sleeper agents, refusal as a feature vector, constitutional AI, and what shipping safely actually requires in 2026.
- [LLM Engineering (12): Production — Deployment, Monitoring, Cost](https://www.chenk.top/en/llm-engineering/12-production/): Serving stack choices in detail, autoscaling LLMs, latency budgets, prompt+completion cost tracking, multi-model routing, FrugalGPT cascading, observability you need from day one, and the on-call patterns that work.

## ML Math Derivations

- [ML Math Derivations (1): Introduction and Mathematical Foundations](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/01-introduction-and-mathematical-foundations/): Why can machines learn from data at all? This first chapter builds the mathematical theory of learning from first principles -- problem formalization, loss surrogates, PAC learning, VC dimension, the bias-variance decomposition and the No Free Lunch theorem.
- [ML Math Derivations (2): Linear Algebra and Matrix Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/02-linear-algebra-and-matrix-theory/): The language of machine learning is linear algebra. This article derives vector spaces, eigendecomposition, SVD, and matrix calculus from first principles -- every tool you need for ML optimization.
- [ML Math Derivations (3): Probability Theory and Statistical Inference](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/03-probability-theory-and-statistical-inference/): Machine learning is uncertainty modeling. This article derives probability spaces, common distributions, MLE, Bayesian estimation, limit theorems and information theory -- the statistical engine behind every ML model.
- [ML Math Derivations (4): Convex Optimization Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/04-convex-optimization-theory/): Nearly every ML algorithm is an optimization problem. This article derives convex sets, convex functions, gradient descent, Newton's method, KKT conditions, and ADMM -- the optimization toolkit for machine learning.
- [ML Math Derivations (5): Linear Regression](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/05-linear-regression/): A complete derivation of linear regression from three perspectives -- algebra (the normal equation), geometry (orthogonal projection), and probability (maximum likelihood) -- followed by Ridge, Lasso, gradient methods, and diagnostics, with every claim verified against scikit-learn.
- [ML Math Derivations (6): Logistic Regression and Classification](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/06-logistic-regression-and-classification/): Complete derivation of logistic regression from sigmoid to softmax, cross-entropy loss, gradient computation, regularization, and multi-class extension with Python verification.
- [ML Math Derivations (7): Decision Trees](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/07-decision-trees/): From information entropy to the Gini index, from ID3 to CART — a complete derivation of decision-tree mathematics: split criteria, continuous and missing values, pruning, and feature importance, with sklearn-verified figures.
- [ML Math Derivations (8): Support Vector Machines](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/08-support-vector-machines/): Complete SVM derivation from maximum margin to Lagrangian duality, KKT conditions, soft margin, kernel trick, and SMO algorithm with step-by-step proofs and Python code.
- [ML Math Derivations (9): Naive Bayes](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/09-naive-bayes/): Rigorous derivation of Naive Bayes from Bayes theorem through conditional independence, parameter estimation, Laplace smoothing, three model variants, and why it works despite violated assumptions.
- [ML Math Derivations (10): Semi-Naive Bayes and Bayesian Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/10-semi-naive-bayes-and-bayesian-networks/): From SPODE, TAN and AODE to full Bayesian networks: how relaxing the conditional-independence assumption -- through one-dependence trees, ensembles of super-parents and graphical structure learning -- closes the gap between Naive Bayes and the full joint distribution.
- [ML Math Derivations (11): Ensemble Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/11-ensemble-learning/): Derive why combining weak learners produces strong ones. Covers bias-variance decomposition, Bagging/Random Forest variance reduction, AdaBoost exponential loss, and GBDT gradient optimization in function space.
- [ML Math Derivations (12): XGBoost and LightGBM](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/12-xgboost-and-lightgbm/): Derive XGBoost's second-order Taylor expansion, regularised objective and split-gain formula, then explore LightGBM's histogram algorithm, GOSS sampling and EFB bundling for industrial-scale gradient boosting.
- [ML Math Derivations (13): EM Algorithm and GMM](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/13-em-algorithm-and-gmm/): Derive the EM algorithm from Jensen's inequality and the ELBO, prove its monotone-ascent guarantee, and apply it to Gaussian Mixture Models with full E-step / M-step formulas, model selection via BIC/AIC, and the K-means correspondence.
- [ML Math Derivations (14): Variational Inference and Variational EM](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/14-variational-inference-and-variational-em/): A first-principles derivation of variational inference. From the ELBO identity and the mean-field assumption to the CAVI updates, variational EM, and the reparameterization trick that powers VAEs.
- [ML Math Derivations (15): Hidden Markov Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/15-hidden-markov-models/): Derive the three classical HMM algorithms from one principle (factorising the joint, then sharing sub-computations across time): Forward-Backward for evaluation and smoothing, Viterbi for MAP decoding, and Baum-Welch (EM) for parameter learning.
- [ML Math Derivations (16): Conditional Random Fields](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/16-conditional-random-fields/): Why do CRFs outperform HMMs on sequence labeling? This article derives linear-chain CRF from the ground up -- potential functions, the forward-backward algorithm, gradient computation, and Viterbi decoding.
- [ML Math Derivations (17): Dimensionality Reduction and PCA](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/17-dimensionality-reduction-and-pca/): High-dimensional spaces are hostile to distance-based learning. This article derives PCA from two equivalent angles (max variance and min reconstruction error), and extends to kernel PCA, LDA, t-SNE, and ICA -- with figures that show what each method actually does to the same data.
- [ML Math Derivations (18): Clustering Algorithms](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/18-clustering-algorithms/): How do you find groups in unlabeled data? This article derives K-means (Lloyd + K-means++), hierarchical, DBSCAN, spectral, and GMM clustering from their mathematical foundations, with seven figures that show why each algorithm encodes a different prior.
- [ML Math Derivations (19): Neural Networks and Backpropagation](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/19-neural-networks-and-backpropagation/): How does a neural network learn? This article derives forward propagation, the chain rule mechanics of backpropagation, vanishing/exploding gradients, and initialization strategies (Xavier, He).
- [ML Math Derivations (20): Regularization and Model Selection](https://www.chenk.top/en/ml-math-derivations/20-regularization-and-model-selection/): The series finale: from the bias-variance decomposition to L1/L2 geometry, dropout as a sub-network sampler, k-fold CV, AIC/BIC, VC bounds, and the modern double-descent phenomenon that broke classical theory.

## NLP

- [NLP (1): Introduction and Text Preprocessing](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/introduction-and-preprocessing/): A first-principles introduction to NLP and text preprocessing. We trace the four eras of the field, build the cleaning to vectorization pipeline by hand, and unpack the math behind tokenization, TF-IDF, n-grams, and distributed representations.
- [NLP (2): Word Embeddings and Language Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/word-embeddings-lm/): Understand how Word2Vec, GloVe, and FastText turn words into vectors that capture meaning. Learn the math, train your own embeddings with Gensim, and connect embeddings to language models.
- [NLP (3): RNN and Sequence Modeling](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/rnn-sequence-modeling/): How RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs process sequences with memory. We derive vanishing gradients from first principles, build a character-level text generator, and implement a Seq2Seq translator in PyTorch.
- [NLP (4): Attention Mechanism and Transformer](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/attention-transformer/): From the bottleneck of Seq2Seq to Attention Is All You Need. Build intuition for scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, masking, and assemble a complete Transformer in PyTorch.
- [NLP (5): BERT and Pretrained Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/bert-pretrained-models/): How BERT made bidirectional pretraining the default in NLP. We unpack the architecture, the 80/10/10 masking rule, fine-tuning recipes, and the RoBERTa/ALBERT/ELECTRA family with HuggingFace code.
- [NLP (6): GPT and Generative Language Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/gpt-generative-models/): From GPT-1 to GPT-4: understand autoregressive language modeling, decoding strategies (greedy, beam search, top-k, top-p), in-context learning, and build a chatbot with HuggingFace.
- [NLP (7): Prompt Engineering and In-Context Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/prompt-engineering-icl/): From prompt anatomy to chain-of-thought, self-consistency and ReAct: a working theory of in-context learning, the variance you have to fight, and the patterns that scale to real systems.
- [NLP (8): Model Fine-tuning and PEFT](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/fine-tuning-peft/): A deep dive into Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning. Why LoRA's low-rank update works, the math and memory accounting behind QLoRA, how Adapters and Prefix-Tuning differ, and how to choose between them in production.
- [NLP (9): Deep Dive into LLM Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/llm-architecture-deep-dive/): Inside modern LLMs: pre-norm + RMSNorm + SwiGLU + RoPE + GQA, KV cache mechanics, FlashAttention's IO-aware schedule, sparse Mixture-of-Experts, and INT8 / INT4 quantization.
- [NLP (10): RAG and Knowledge Enhancement Systems](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/rag-knowledge-enhancement/): Build production-grade RAG systems from first principles: the retrieve-then-generate decomposition, vector indexes (FAISS / Milvus / Chroma / Weaviate / Pinecone), dense+sparse hybrid retrieval with RRF, cross-encoder reranking, chunking strategies, query rewriting, HyDE, and Self-RAG / Corrective-RAG.
- [NLP (11): Multimodal Large Language Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/multimodal-nlp/): A deep dive into multimodal LLMs: contrastive vision-language pre-training with CLIP, parameter-efficient bridging with BLIP-2's Q-Former, visual instruction tuning with LLaVA, robust speech recognition with Whisper, GPT-4V capabilities, and the MMBench/MME/MMMU benchmark landscape — with reproducible code.
- [NLP (12): Frontiers and Practical Applications](https://www.chenk.top/en/nlp/frontiers-applications/): Series finale: agents and tool use (Function Calling, ReAct), code generation (Code Llama, Codex), long-context attention (Longformer, Infini-attention), reasoning models (o1, R1), safety and alignment, evaluation, and production deployment with FastAPI, vLLM and Docker.

## ODE Foundations

- [Ordinary Differential Equations (1): Origins and Intuition](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/01-origins-and-intuition/): Why do differential equations exist? Starting from cooling coffee and swinging pendulums, build your first ODE intuition and solve one in Python.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (2): First-Order Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/02-first-order-methods/): Master the four main techniques for first-order ODEs: separation of variables, integrating factors, exact equations, and Bernoulli substitution -- with applications to finance, pharmacology, ecology, and circuits.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (3): Higher-Order Linear Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/03-linear-theory/): From springs to RLC circuits, the full theory of higher-order linear ODEs: superposition, the Wronskian, characteristic equations, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, and the resonance phenomenon.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (4): The Laplace Transform](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/04-constant-coefficients/): The engineer's secret weapon: turn differential equations into algebra with the Laplace transform. Learn the key properties, partial fractions, transfer functions, and PID control basics.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (5): Power Series and Special Functions](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/05-laplace-transform/): When elementary functions fail, power series step in. Learn the Frobenius method and meet the special functions of physics: Bessel, Legendre, Hermite, and Airy functions -- with Python visualizations.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (6): Linear Systems and the Matrix Exponential](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/06-power-series/): When multiple variables interact, you need systems of ODEs. Learn the matrix exponential, eigenvalue-based solutions, phase portrait classification, and applications to coupled oscillators and RLC circuits.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (7): Stability Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/07-systems-and-phase-plane/): Will a bridge survive the wind? Will an ecosystem recover from a shock? Stability theory answers these questions using Lyapunov functions, linearization, and bifurcation analysis.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (8): Nonlinear Systems and Phase Portraits](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/08-nonlinear-stability/): Step beyond linearity: predator-prey oscillations, competition exclusion, Van der Pol limit cycles, Hamiltonian systems, and the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem -- the full toolkit for nonlinear 2D dynamics.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (9): Chaos Theory and the Lorenz System](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/09-bifurcation-chaos/): Deterministic yet unpredictable: the Lorenz system, butterfly effect, Lyapunov exponents, strange attractors, and the routes from order to chaos -- with Python simulations throughout.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (10): Bifurcation Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/10-bifurcation-theory/): Bifurcation theory explains how smooth parameter changes cause dramatic qualitative shifts in system behavior. Master saddle-node, transcritical, pitchfork, and Hopf bifurcations through normal forms, stability arguments, and Python visualizations.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (11): Numerical Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/11-numerical-methods/): From Euler's tangent step to Dormand-Prince adaptive integrators: a working numerics toolkit. Convergence orders, A-stability, stiffness, and when to reach for Radau or BDF instead of RK45.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (12): Boundary Value Problems](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/12-boundary-value-problems/): Boundary value problems specify the solution at both ends of an interval. Master shooting, finite differences, collocation, and Sturm-Liouville eigenproblems -- with applications from beam deflection to the quantum harmonic oscillator.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (13): Introduction to Partial Differential Equations](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/13-pde-introduction/): Step from ODEs into partial differential equations. Classify PDEs into parabolic, hyperbolic, and elliptic types. Solve the heat, wave, and Laplace equations using separation of variables and finite differences.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (14): Epidemic Models and Epidemiology](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/14-epidemiology/): Mathematical epidemiology from first principles. Build the SIR and SEIR models, derive R0 and the herd-immunity threshold, fit COVID-style scenarios with asymptomatic transmission and time-varying interventions.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (15): Population Dynamics](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/15-population-dynamics/): Mathematical ecology from single-species to spatial: Malthus, logistic, Allee, Lotka-Volterra predator-prey and competition, age-structured Leslie matrices, metapopulations, and Fisher-KPP traveling waves.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (16): Fundamentals of Control Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/16-control-theory/): Learn how differential equations power control systems. Cover transfer functions, PID controllers, root locus, Bode plots, state-space methods, controllability, observability, pole placement, LQR optimal control, and observer design with Python examples.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (17): Physics and Engineering Applications](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/17-physics-engineering-applications/): See ODEs in action across physics and engineering. Walk through the nonlinear pendulum, RLC circuit and resonance, Kepler orbits and conservation laws, multi-DOF structural vibration with tuned mass dampers, and fluid flow from Poiseuille to vortex shedding -- all with full Python simulations.
- [Ordinary Differential Equations (18): Frontiers and Series Finale](https://www.chenk.top/en/ode/18-advanced-topics-summary/): The series finale. Survey four research frontiers reshaping how we model dynamics -- Neural ODEs, delay equations, stochastic differential equations, and fractional calculus -- then take stock of the entire 18-chapter journey with a method-selection flowchart, the deep ODE-ML connection, and a roadmap for what to study next.

## OpenClaw QuickStart

- [OpenClaw QuickStart (1): What This Thing Actually Is](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/01-what-is-openclaw/): What OpenClaw is, where it sits vs ChatGPT/Claude, and which problems it solves.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (2): Install and First Chat in 10 Minutes](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/02-install-and-first-chat/): Install OpenClaw, plug in a model provider, and have a working agent in ten minutes.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (3): The Six Layers That Make the Agent Loop Work](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/03-architecture/): Gateway, Pi Agent, Tools, Skills, Memory, Channels — what each layer does.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (4): Configuration, Model Providers, and the Coding Plan Trick](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/04-configuration/): openclaw.json walkthrough, model providers, and the Bailian Coding Plan trick.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (5): Wiring Telegram, DingTalk, and the WeChat Reality](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/05-channels/): Telegram in five minutes, DingTalk in fifteen, WeChat via WorkBuddy.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (6): Skills, MCP, and Shipping Something Real](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/06-skills-and-mcp/): Write a Skill, attach a Playwright MCP server, and ship a morning-briefing agent.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (7): The Memory System, Without the Magic](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/07-memory-system/): MEMORY.md as index, memoryFlush, bge-m3 search, and the v2026.3.7 ContextEngine.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (8): Heartbeat, Cron, and Getting Pinged at 7am](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/08-cron-and-heartbeat/): Heartbeat patrols and Cron timers — configs for daily briefings and weekly reports.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (9): The China IM Picker, with Honest Tradeoffs](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/09-china-channels/): DingTalk, WeCom, WeChat WorkBuddy — a picker matrix with actual config blocks.
- [OpenClaw QuickStart (10): Production Deploy and the Failure Modes Nobody Warns You About](https://www.chenk.top/en/openclaw-quickstart/10-production-deploy/): ECS, pm2, nginx, acme.sh — plus eight production failure modes and their fixes.

## Optimization Theory

- [Optimization (1): Convex Analysis Foundations](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/01-convex-analysis-foundations/): The geometric and analytic toolkit that unlocks the rest of the series: convex sets, convex functions, the conjugate (Fenchel) transform, subgradients, and the indicator/support function pair. Includes complete proofs of Jensen's inequality, the projection theorem, and the subdifferential of basic norms.
- [Optimization (2): Smoothness, Strong Convexity, and Nesterov Acceleration](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/02-smoothness-strong-convexity-nesterov/): Three concepts that demystify most of optimization: Lipschitz smoothness fixes the maximum step size, strong convexity sets the convergence rate and uniqueness of the minimizer, and Nesterov acceleration replaces kappa with sqrt(kappa) without sacrificing stability. Includes the key theorems with proofs and a least-squares experiment.
- [Optimization (3): The Gradient Descent Family from SGD to AdamW](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/03-gradient-descent-family/): One article that traces the full lineage GD -> SGD -> Momentum -> NAG -> AdaGrad -> RMSProp -> Adam -> AdamW, then onwards to Lion / Sophia / Schedule-Free. Each step is framed by the specific failure of the previous one, and we end with a practical selection guide.
- [Optimization (4): Learning Rate and Schedules](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/04-learning-rate-schedules/): A practitioner's guide to the single most important hyperparameter: why too-large LR explodes, how warmup and schedules really work, the LR range test, the LR-batch-size-weight-decay coupling, and recent ideas like WSD, Schedule-Free AdamW, and D-Adaptation.
- [Optimization (5): Acceleration Beyond Nesterov](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/05-acceleration-beyond-nesterov/): What does it really mean for a first-order method to be optimal? We prove a tight lower bound matching Nesterov's rate, derive Polyak's Heavy-Ball method as the continuous-time limit, build a unified Lyapunov framework that covers both, and show how the Catalyst meta-algorithm bootstraps any solver to the accelerated rate.
- [Optimization (6): Composite Optimization and Proximal Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/06-composite-proximal-methods/): A systematic walk through the proximal operator: convex-analysis basics, the Moreau envelope, closed-form proxes, and how they power ISTA, FISTA, ADMM, LASSO, and SVM in practice.
- [Optimization (7): Second-Order Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/07-second-order-methods/): Second-order methods break the sqrt(kappa) barrier by using curvature. We prove Newton's quadratic local convergence, derive BFGS from a secant condition + low-rank update, walk through L-BFGS's two-loop recursion that makes it the workhorse for medium-scale ML, and analyze trust-region subproblems with the dogleg solution.
- [Optimization (8): Lagrangian Duality and KKT Conditions](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/08-lagrangian-duality-kkt/): How constraints become prices: the Lagrangian, weak duality, Slater's condition for strong duality, the KKT system as necessary and sufficient optimality, and why the SVM dual is much smaller than the SVM primal. Includes complete proofs and the saddle-point characterization.
- [Optimization (9): Interior-Point Methods and Self-Concordant Barriers](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/09-interior-point-barrier/): How interior-point methods became the default solver for convex programming: replace inequalities with a logarithmic barrier, parametrize the central path, and apply Newton's method. Includes the self-concordance machinery and the proof of the celebrated O(sqrt(n) log(1/eps)) iteration complexity.
- [Optimization (10): Stochastic Optimization and Variance Reduction](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/10-stochastic-variance-reduction/): Why does SGD work? We prove the O(1/sqrt(T)) convex rate and the O(1/(mu T)) strongly convex rate from the gradient noise budget. Then variance reduction: SVRG, SAGA, Katyusha — methods that get to the linear rate of full GD using stochastic samples, with complete analysis of why they work.
- [Optimization (11): Non-Convex Optimization and Saddle Escape](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/11-nonconvex-saddle-escape/): Why does SGD work for training neural networks despite the non-convex landscape? We prove perturbed GD escapes strict saddles in polynomial time, derive convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and survey what is provably known about deep learning loss surfaces — over-parameterization, NTK, and the implicit bias toward flat minima.
- [Optimization (12): Discrete and Global Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/optimization-theory/12-discrete-global-optimization/): When variables are integer-valued or the problem is non-convex with multiple basins, classical convex methods stop working. This article surveys what does work: integer programming via branch-and-bound, LP relaxation gap analysis, the heuristic taxonomy (PSO, GA, SOA, simulated annealing), and a deep walk-through of the Spiral Optimization Algorithm applied to constrained mean-variance portfolio optimization.

## PDE and Machine Learning

- [PDE and ML (1): Physics-Informed Neural Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/01-physics-informed-neural-networks/): From finite differences to PINNs: automatic differentiation, PDE residual losses, NTK-based training pathologies, Burgers inverse problems, and a side-by-side comparison with FEM and neural operators. Seven figures included.
- [PDE and ML (2): Neural Operator Theory](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/02-neural-operator-theory/): DeepONet vs FNO from a function-space view: resolution invariance, error bounds, failure modes.
- [PDE and ML (3): Variational Principles and Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/03-variational-principles/): Calculus of variations to Wasserstein gradient flow and the mean-field limit of neural networks.
- [PDE and ML (4): Variational Inference and the Fokker-Planck Equation](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/04-variational-inference/): Variational inference and Langevin MCMC are two faces of the same Fokker-Planck PDE. We derive the equivalence, build SVGD as an interacting-particle approximation, and quantify convergence under log-Sobolev inequalities.
- [PDE and ML (5): Symplectic Geometry and Structure-Preserving Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/05-symplectic-geometry/): Standard neural networks violate conservation laws. This article derives Hamiltonian mechanics, symplectic integrators, HNNs, LNNs, and SympNets from the geometry of phase space.
- [PDE and ML (6): Continuous Normalizing Flows and Neural ODE](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/06-continuous-normalizing-flows/): How do you turn a Gaussian into a complex data distribution?
