This article derives Neural ODEs, the adjoint method, continuous normalizing flows (FFJORD), and Flow Matching from the underlying ODE/PDE theory, and shows the seven core mechanisms in pictures.
- [PDE and ML (7): Diffusion Models and Score Matching](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/07-diffusion-models/): Diffusion models are PDE solvers in disguise. We derive the heat equation, Fokker-Planck, score matching, DDPM, and DDIM from a unified PDE perspective and visualise every step.
- [PDE and ML (8): Reaction-Diffusion Systems and Graph Neural Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/pde-ml/08-reaction-diffusion-systems/): Deep GNNs collapse because they are diffusion equations on graphs. Turing's reaction-diffusion theory tells us how to fix it -- and closes the eight-chapter PDE+ML series.

## Personal Finance

- [Personal Finance (1): Why Asset Allocation Matters](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/01-why-allocation/): Why your money shouldn't all sit in one place, and what 'allocation' actually means, from an engineer who just worked it out.
- [Personal Finance (2): The Product Zoo — From Money Market Funds to Gold](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/02-product-zoo/): A field guide to every financial product a beginner meets in a Chinese wealth-management app — what each one does, and where the risk hides.
- [Personal Finance (3): What a Bank Wealth-Management Subsidiary (理财子) Really Is](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/03-wealth-mgmt-subs/): Post-2018 bank wealth management in China: net-value products, R1-R5 risk levels, fixed income+, and how to actually read a product prospectus.
- [Personal Finance (4): Index Funds and ETFs — The Lazy Investor's Edge](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/04-index-funds/): Why most people should just buy the index — the fee-drag math, the Chinese index landscape, and how dollar-cost averaging actually works.
- [Personal Finance (5): Bonds and Fixed Income — The Stable Half of Your Portfolio](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/05-bonds-fixed-income/): Bonds without the padding: yield, duration, why prices fall when rates rise, and what November 2022 taught me about "safe" money.
- [Personal Finance (6): From Theory to Practice — A Beginner's Portfolio Path](https://www.chenk.top/en/personal-finance/06-portfolio-practice/): The practical capstone: allocation tables by portfolio size, dollar-cost averaging steps, a rebalancing rule with a worked example, behavioral traps, and where I actually am.

## Probability and Statistics

- [Probability and Statistics (1): Probability Spaces — Why We Need Axioms (But Won't Overdo It)](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/01-probability-foundations/): Building probability from the ground up: sample spaces, Kolmogorov's axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, and the birthday problem — with proofs and Python simulations.
- [Probability and Statistics (2): Random Variables and the Distributions That Matter](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/02-random-variables/): A rigorous tour of random variables, PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, and every distribution that matters in practice — Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Gaussian, Exponential, Gamma, and Beta — with derivations, proofs, and Python visualizations.
- [Probability and Statistics (3): Expectation, Variance, and the Moment-Generating Trick](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/03-expectation-and-moments/): From expectation and variance through covariance, correlation, and moment-generating functions to Chebyshev's inequality — the complete toolkit for summarizing random variables, with proofs for every result.
- [Probability and Statistics (4): Joint Distributions, Marginalization, and Independence](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/04-joint-distributions/): Joint PMFs and PDFs, marginal and conditional distributions, the bivariate normal, transformations via the Jacobian method, convolutions, and order statistics — with proofs and contour plot visualizations.
- [Probability and Statistics (5): Law of Large Numbers and the Central Limit Theorem](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/05-limit-theorems/): The two pillars of probability: the Law of Large Numbers guarantees sample means converge, and the Central Limit Theorem explains why everything looks Gaussian — with proofs, convergence concepts, and Python simulations.
- [Probability and Statistics (6): Estimation — MLE, MAP, and the Bias-Variance Story](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/06-estimation-theory/): Point estimation from method of moments through maximum likelihood and MAP, with Fisher information, the Cramer-Rao bound, and the bias-variance decomposition that explains overfitting and underfitting.
- [Probability and Statistics (7): Hypothesis Testing — p-Values, Confidence Intervals, and All Their Pitfalls](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/07-hypothesis-testing/): A rigorous treatment of hypothesis testing, p-values, Type I/II errors, confidence intervals, and multiple testing corrections — including the misinterpretations that trip up even experienced practitioners, with Python implementations.
- [Probability and Statistics (8): Bayesian Statistics — Priors, Posteriors, and Why Frequentists Argue](https://www.chenk.top/en/probability-statistics/08-bayesian-thinking/): Bayesian inference from first principles: posterior distributions, conjugate priors, the Beta-Binomial and Normal-Normal models, credible intervals, predictive distributions, MCMC intuition, and deep connections to machine learning regularization.

## Product Thinking

- [Product Thinking (1): Architecture Design — From Monolith to Autonomous Agents](https://www.chenk.top/en/product-thinking/01-architecture/): How my architectural thinking evolved from a single Next.js app to distributed autonomous agent systems — and the patterns that emerged along the way.
- [Product Thinking (2): Security Engineering — Defense Without Paranoia](https://www.chenk.top/en/product-thinking/02-security/): How I learned to build security into the system itself — pre-commit hooks, atomic guards, two-layer firewalls, and the art of automated defense.
- [Product Thinking (3): UX & Design Systems — Tokens, Dark Mode, and Bilingual](https://www.chenk.top/en/product-thinking/03-ux-design/): Building a design system from CSS tokens to dark mode to bilingual content — and why consistency matters more than creativity.
- [Product Thinking (4): Self-Healing Systems — Teaching Machines to Fix Themselves](https://www.chenk.top/en/product-thinking/04-self-healing/): The philosophy and engineering of systems that detect, diagnose, and fix their own failures — from watchdog anti-patterns to autonomous improvement engines.
- [Product Thinking (5): Abstraction Thinking — From Math to Systems](https://www.chenk.top/en/product-thinking/05-abstraction/): How a math background shapes engineering decisions — from group theory to FSMs, from proof structure to API design, and why 700 articles is an abstraction engine.

## Python Engineering

- [Python Engineering (1): Environment Setup — pyenv, venv, and Dependency Hell](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/01-environment-and-toolchain/): Master Python environment management with pyenv, virtual environments, and modern dependency tools. Escape dependency hell for good.
- [Python Engineering (2): Project Structure — From Script to Package](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/02-project-structure/): Learn how to organize Python code into proper packages with imports, entry points, and CLI tools. Build a real command-line application from scratch.
- [Python Engineering (3): Testing — pytest, Fixtures, and the Confidence Loop](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/03-testing-and-debugging/): Build confidence in your code with pytest fixtures, parametrize, mocking, and coverage. Learn debugging techniques that save hours.
- [Python Engineering (4): Type Hints, Linting, and Code Quality](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/04-type-hints-and-linting/): Add type safety with mypy, enforce style with ruff and black, and automate checks with pre-commit hooks. Make code reviews about logic, not formatting.
- [Python Engineering (5): I/O, Serialization, and Data Formats](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/05-io-and-serialization/): Handle files, paths, encodings, and data formats in Python. Compare JSON, YAML, TOML, CSV, pickle, and Parquet with practical examples.
- [Python Engineering (6): Concurrency — Threads, Processes, and asyncio](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/06-concurrency/): Understand the GIL, master threading, multiprocessing, and asyncio. Learn which concurrency model to use for I/O-bound vs CPU-bound workloads.
- [Python Engineering (7): Packaging — From pip install to PyPI](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/07-packaging-and-distribution/): Package your Python code for distribution via pip, publish to PyPI, create Docker images, and manage versioning. The complete guide from local project to installable package.
- [Python Engineering (8): Performance — Profiling, Caching, and Knowing When to Stop](https://www.chenk.top/en/python-engineering/08-performance-and-profiling/): Profile Python code to find real bottlenecks, apply caching and vectorization where they matter, and avoid the trap of premature optimization.

## Recommendation Systems

- [Recommendation Systems (1): Fundamentals and Core Concepts](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/01-fundamentals/): A beginner-friendly guide to recommendation systems: the three core paradigms (collaborative filtering, content-based, hybrid), evaluation metrics, the multi-stage funnel architecture used in production, and the open challenges of cold-start, sparsity, and the long tail. With working Python implementations.
- [Recommendation Systems (2): Collaborative Filtering and Matrix Factorization](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/02-collaborative-filtering/): An in-depth tour of collaborative filtering and matrix factorization: User-CF and Item-CF, similarity metrics, latent-factor models, SVD++, ALS, BPR, and factorization machines — with intuitions, derivations, and runnable Python.
- [Recommendation Systems (3): Deep Learning Foundations](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/03-deep-learning-basics/): From MLPs to embeddings to NeuMF, YouTube DNN, and Wide & Deep -- a progressive walkthrough of the deep learning building blocks that power every modern recommender, with verified architectures and runnable PyTorch code.
- [Recommendation Systems (4): CTR Prediction and Click-Through Rate Modeling](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/04-ctr-prediction/): A practical guide to CTR prediction models -- from Logistic Regression and Factorization Machines to DeepFM, xDeepFM, DCN, AutoInt, and FiBiNet -- with intuitive explanations and PyTorch implementations.
- [Recommendation Systems (5): Embedding and Representation Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/05-embedding-techniques/): How modern recommenders learn dense vector representations for users and items: Word2Vec / Item2Vec, Node2Vec, two-tower DSSM and YouTube DNN, negative sampling, FAISS/HNSW serving, and how to evaluate embedding quality. Concept, math, code and production guidance in one place.
- [Recommendation Systems (6): Sequential Recommendation and Session-based Modeling](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/06-sequential-recommendation/): How recommenders use the order of user actions to predict the next one. Markov chains, GRU4Rec, Caser, SASRec, BERT4Rec, BST, and SR-GNN, with implementations and intuition.
- [Recommendation Systems (7): Graph Neural Networks and Social Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/07-graph-neural-networks/): A deep, intuition-first walkthrough of graph neural networks for recommendation: GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, PinSage, LightGCN, NGCF, social signals, scalable sampling, and cold start. Diagrams plus working PyTorch.
- [Recommendation Systems (8): Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/08-knowledge-graph/): Learn how knowledge graphs supercharge recommendation systems by adding semantic understanding. Covers RippleNet, KGCN, KGAT, CKE, and path-based reasoning -- with intuitive explanations, real-world analogies, and working Python code.
- [Recommendation Systems (9): Multi-Task Learning and Multi-Objective Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/09-multi-task-learning/): How real recommenders juggle clicks, conversions, watch time and revenue at once. Shared-Bottom, ESMM, MMoE, PLE explained from first principles, with PyTorch code, loss-balancing strategies and the gradient-conflict story behind them.
- [Recommendation Systems (10): Deep Interest Networks and Attention Mechanisms](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/10-deep-interest-networks/): From DIN's target attention to DIEN's AUGRU and BST's Transformer — how Alibaba taught CTR models to read a user's history like a chef reads the room.
- [Recommendation Systems (11): Contrastive Learning and Self-Supervised Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/11-contrastive-learning/): A practitioner's guide to contrastive learning for recommendations: InfoNCE and the role of temperature, SimCLR vs MoCo negatives, SGL graph augmentations, CL4SRec sequence augmentations, XSimGCL's noise-only trick, with intuition, math, and clean PyTorch.
- [Recommendation Systems (12): Large Language Models and Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/12-llm-recommendation/): How LLMs reshape recommendation: enhancers (P5, M6Rec), predictors (TallRec, GenRec), and agents (LlamaRec, ChatREC). Hybrid pipelines, cold-start wins, prompt design, and the cost/quality Pareto frontier.
- [Recommendation Systems (13): Fairness, Debiasing, and Explainability](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/13-fairness-explainability/): A practical deep dive into trustworthy recommendation: the seven biases (popularity, position, selection, exposure, conformity, demographic, confirmation), causal inference (RCTs, IPS, doubly robust estimators), debiasing in production (MACR, DICE, FairCo), and explainability (LIME, SHAP, counterfactuals).
- [Recommendation Systems (14): Cross-Domain Recommendation and Cold-Start Solutions](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/14-cross-domain-cold-start/): Cold-start and cross-domain recommendation in depth: the three faces of cold-start, EMCDR/PTUPCDR cross-domain bridges, MeLU/MAML meta-learning, UCB bandits for exploration, and the cold-to-warm production stack.
- [Recommendation Systems (15): Real-Time Recommendation and Online Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/15-real-time-online/): A practitioner's guide to real-time recommendation: streaming pipelines (Kafka + Flink), online learning (SGD, FTRL, AdaGrad), bandits (UCB, Thompson Sampling, LinUCB), latency budgets, feature freshness, concept drift, and the cache-vs-compute trade-off you actually tune in production.
- [Recommendation Systems (16): Industrial Architecture and Best Practices](https://www.chenk.top/en/recommendation-systems/16-industrial-practice/): Production recommendation systems serve hundreds of millions of users with sub-100ms latency. This final article covers the industrial multi-stage pipeline (recall, coarse ranking, fine ranking, reranking), feature stores, A/B testing, model optimization, deployment, and team responsibilities -- drawing on patterns from YouTube, TikTok, Taobao, and ByteDance.

## Reinforcement Learning

- [Reinforcement Learning (1): Fundamentals and Core Concepts](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/01-fundamentals-and-core-concepts/): A beginner-friendly guide to the mathematical foundations of reinforcement learning -- MDPs, Bellman equations, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo methods, and temporal difference learning -- with working Python code, all explained through the analogy of learning to ride a bicycle.
- [Reinforcement Learning (2): Q-Learning and Deep Q-Networks (DQN)](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/02-q-learning-and-dqn/): How DQN combined neural networks with Q-Learning to master Atari games -- covering experience replay, target networks, Double DQN, Dueling DQN, Prioritized Experience Replay, and Rainbow.
- [Reinforcement Learning (3): Policy Gradient and Actor-Critic Methods](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/03-policy-gradient-and-actor-critic/): From REINFORCE to SAC -- how policy gradient methods directly optimize policies, naturally handle continuous actions, and power modern algorithms like PPO, TD3, and SAC.
- [Reinforcement Learning (4): Exploration Strategies and Curiosity-Driven Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/04-exploration-and-curiosity-driven-learning/): How do RL agents discover rewards when the environment gives almost no feedback? From count-based methods to ICM, RND, and NGU -- the science of curiosity-driven exploration.
- [Reinforcement Learning (5): Model-Based RL and World Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/05-model-based-rl-and-world-models/): From Dyna and MBPO to World Models, Dreamer, and MuZero -- how learning a model lets agents plan in imagination and reach expert performance with 10-100x fewer real interactions.
- [Reinforcement Learning (6): PPO and TRPO — Trust Region Policy Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/06-ppo-and-trpo/): Why PPO became the most widely used RL algorithm -- from TRPO's theoretical foundations through natural gradients to PPO's elegant clipping mechanism, plus its role in RLHF for large language models.
- [Reinforcement Learning (7): Imitation Learning and Inverse RL](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/07-imitation-learning/): A practical, theory-grounded tour of imitation learning: behavioral cloning and its quadratic compounding error, DAgger and the no-regret reduction, MaxEnt inverse RL for recovering reward functions, and adversarial methods (GAIL, AIRL). Includes runnable PyTorch code, a method-selection ladder, and seven publication-quality figures.
- [Reinforcement Learning (8): AlphaGo and Monte Carlo Tree Search](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/08-alphago-and-mcts/): From MCTS to AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, and MuZero. Understand UCT exploration-exploitation, self-play training, and planning with learned models. Includes a complete AlphaZero implementation for Gomoku.
- [Reinforcement Learning (9): Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/09-multi-agent-rl/): A working tour of multi-agent RL: Markov games, the non-stationarity and credit-assignment problems, CTDE, value decomposition (VDN, QMIX), counterfactual baselines (COMA), MADDPG, communication topologies, and the league-training pipeline behind AlphaStar and OpenAI Five — with a runnable QMIX mixer in PyTorch.
- [Reinforcement Learning (10): Offline Reinforcement Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/10-offline-reinforcement-learning/): Master offline RL: learn policies from fixed datasets without environment interaction. Covers distributional shift, Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), BCQ, Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), Decision Transformer, with a complete CQL implementation.
- [Reinforcement Learning (11): Hierarchical RL and Meta-Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/11-hierarchical-and-meta-rl/): A deep dive into hierarchical RL (Options, MAXQ, Feudal Networks, goal-conditioned policies) and meta-RL (MAML, FOMAML, RL^2). Covers temporal abstraction, semi-MDPs, manager-worker architectures, second-order meta-gradients and recurrent meta-learners, with annotated PyTorch implementations.
- [Reinforcement Learning (12): RLHF and LLM Applications](https://www.chenk.top/en/reinforcement-learning/12-rlhf-and-llm-applications/): How RLHF turned base language models into ChatGPT and Claude: the SFT→Reward-Model→PPO pipeline, the Bradley-Terry preference model, the DPO closed-form derivation, RLAIF and Constitutional AI, reward hacking and Goodhart's law, and where RL goes next in embodied intelligence.

## Field Notes on Reliable Agents

- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (1): The Build Is the Only Gate](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/01-build-is-the-gate/): Three agents each edited their slice of a TypeScript repo, each ran tsc on its own files, each reported green. The merged tree failed to compile in eight seconds. The fix is one rule: only the orchestrator's full build counts as done.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (2): Safety Nets Beat Flaky Observers](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/02-safety-nets/): Probabilistic triggers — IntersectionObservers, LLM judgments, event listeners — fail silently and leave you with invisible content or stuck state. The fix is a deterministic fallback behind every unreliable observer, plus one hard rule: the rendered output is ground truth, not the observer's opinion.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (3): Charge Before You Produce](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/03-charge-before-produce/): When an agent step costs money or mutates shared state, the order in which you write matters more than the step itself. Charge before you produce, reset counters before the call, and make every mutation survive a crash at the worst possible moment.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (4): Deployed Is Not Executed](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/04-deployed-not-executed/): The most seductive lie in shipping software: 'I deployed it, so it works.' Code can ship, sit there, and never run on the path you think it runs on. Two failure modes — built-but-not-wired, and deployed-but-not-executed — and how to prove the feature actually fires.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (5): Autonomy That Won't Nuke the Wrong Thing](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/05-autonomy-safety/): Autonomous cleanup and self-healing are the whole point of agents — and also the fastest way to delete the wrong data. The resolution: act only on exact recorded identities, verify counts against reality before any destructive step, and interrogate the signal before you trust it.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (6): Re-Verify the Old Fixes Every Round](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/06-reverify-old-fixes/): In a long-running optimization loop, the most dangerous regression is the one that quietly re-breaks something you already fixed. The habit that prevents it: every round, re-verify the prior fixes on their real trigger paths — not just the new change.
- [Field Notes on Reliable Agents (7): Turn Every Scar Into a Rule](https://www.chenk.top/en/reliable-agents/07-distill-lessons/): The final discipline that makes all the others compound: after every fix, distill the lesson into a form the system itself can consume — a test, a scan rule, a safe-pattern — so the scar becomes automation that prevents the next occurrence, instead of tribal knowledge you re-learn the hard way.

## System Design

- [System Design (1): Thinking in Systems — Load, Latency, and the Art of Estimation](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/01-thinking-in-systems/): Learn the foundational skills of system design: back-of-envelope estimation, availability math, SLA definitions, and a repeatable framework for tackling any design problem.
- [System Design (2): DNS, CDN, and Load Balancing — The First Three Hops](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/02-dns-cdn-load-balancing/): Every web request begins with DNS resolution, may traverse a CDN edge, and lands on a load balancer before reaching your application. Understanding these three hops is essential to building systems that are fast, reliable, and globally distributed.
- [System Design (3): API Design — REST, gRPC, GraphQL, and Choosing Wisely](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/03-api-design/): A practical comparison of REST, gRPC, and GraphQL — covering protocol design, real-world trade-offs, rate limiting algorithms, idempotency, and a decision framework for choosing the right API style.
- [System Design (4): Caching — Where to Cache, What to Evict, and When Caching Hurts](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/04-caching-strategies/): A deep dive into caching strategies across every layer of the stack — from CDN to database buffer pools — covering cache-aside, write-through, write-behind patterns, eviction policies, thundering herd mitigation, and practical Redis configurations.
- [System Design (5): Message Queues and Event-Driven Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/05-message-queues/): A practical guide to message queues and event-driven systems — covering Kafka and RabbitMQ architectures, delivery guarantees, event sourcing, CQRS, dead letter queues, backpressure, and a complete order processing pipeline design.
- [System Design (6): Microservices vs Monoliths — The Honest Tradeoff](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/06-microservices-vs-monoliths/): An honest assessment of monoliths vs microservices — covering the distributed systems tax, service boundary design with DDD, inter-service communication patterns, circuit breakers, service mesh, API gateways, and a practical decision framework.
- [System Design (7): Data Pipelines — Batch, Stream, and the Lambda Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/07-data-pipelines/): A practical guide to data pipeline architectures — covering ETL vs ELT, batch processing with Spark, stream processing with Flink, Lambda vs Kappa architectures, Change Data Capture, and a complete real-time analytics pipeline design.
- [System Design (8): Case Studies — URL Shortener, Chat System, News Feed](https://www.chenk.top/en/system-design/08-case-studies/): Three complete system design walkthroughs — a URL shortener, a real-time chat system, and a news feed — each following the full process from requirements and estimation through high-level design, deep dives, and scaling strategies.

## Terraform Agents

- [Terraform for AI Agents (1): Why IaC Is the Only Sane Way to Ship Agents](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/01-why-terraform-for-agents/): Agent systems are a moving target — new tools, new memory stores, new regions every month. Manual console clicks don't survive the second teammate. This first article makes the case for Terraform on Alibaba Cloud, surveys what the alicloud provider actually covers, and compares it to Pulumi, Crossplane, and ROS so you pick the right tool the first time.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (2): Provider, Auth, and Remote State on OSS](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/02-provider-and-state-setup/): Pinning the alicloud provider, picking between AK/SK, AssumeRole, and ECS RAM role auth, putting tfstate on OSS with Tablestore locking, and the workspace pattern that keeps dev/staging/prod from stomping each other. Plus the dozen failure modes that bite first-timers.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (3): A Reusable VPC and Security Baseline](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/03-vpc-and-security-baseline/): The first reusable module — a three-zone VPC with public/private subnets, NAT egress, security groups layered by tier, and KMS keys per data domain. The same code shows up in every agent stack I've shipped, parameterised but otherwise unchanged.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (4): Compute — ECS, ACK, or Function Compute?](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/04-compute-for-agent-runtime/): The three places an agent's main loop can live on Aliyun: a long-running ECS instance with pm2, a Kubernetes pod on ACK, or a Function Compute invocation. The cost-crossover model I use to pick between them, and a real cloud-init bootstrap that goes from bare Ubuntu to running agent in 90 seconds.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (5): Storage — Vector, Relational, and Object Memory](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/05-storage-for-agent-memory/): An agent has three kinds of memory and they map onto three Aliyun services: PolarDB/RDS for sessions, OpenSearch (vector edition) or pgvector for embeddings, OSS for artifacts. Real Terraform for each, plus the lifecycle and backup rules that keep the bill flat.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (6): LLM Gateway and Secrets Management](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/06-llm-gateway-and-secrets/): Centralise LLM API access through one gateway: per-agent quotas, request logging, and zero secrets outside KMS. Terraform-provisioned API Gateway plus self-hosted LiteLLM on ECS, with DashScope/OpenAI/Anthropic keys rotating automatically through KMS Secrets Manager.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (7): Observability, SLS Dashboards, and Cost Alarms](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/07-observability-and-cost-control/): Logs to SLS, traces to ARMS, metrics to CloudMonitor — all provisioned in HCL so a new env comes pre-instrumented. The four alarms that actually catch real incidents and the SLS-driven cost dashboard that tells you which agent is burning your budget before payday.
- [Terraform for AI Agents (8): End-to-End — research-agent-stack in One Apply](https://www.chenk.top/en/terraform-agents/08-end-to-end-walkthrough/): Stitching the seven modules into one repo, running terraform apply once, and watching a complete agent runtime — VPC, ECS, RDS, OpenSearch, OSS, LLM gateway, SLS observability, cost alarms — come up in seven minutes. Real apply output, the module DAG, full prod cost arithmetic, and the starter repo to fork.

## Time Series Forecasting

- [Time Series Forecasting (1): Traditional Statistical Models](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/01-traditional-models/): ARIMA, SARIMA, VAR, GARCH, Prophet, exponential smoothing and the Kalman filter, derived from a single state-space view. With Box-Jenkins workflow, ACF/PACF identification, and runnable Python.
- [Time Series Forecasting (2): LSTM — Gate Mechanisms and Long-Term Dependencies](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/lstm/): How LSTM's forget, input, and output gates solve the vanishing gradient problem. Complete PyTorch code for time series forecasting with practical tuning tips.
- [Time Series Forecasting (3): GRU — Lightweight Gates and Efficiency Trade-offs](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/gru/): GRU distills LSTM into two gates for faster training and 25% fewer parameters. Learn when GRU beats LSTM, with formulas, benchmarks, PyTorch code, and a decision matrix.
- [Time Series Forecasting (4): Attention Mechanisms — Direct Long-Range Dependencies](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/attention-mechanism/): Self-attention, multi-head attention, and positional encoding for time series. Step-by-step math, PyTorch implementations, and visualization techniques for interpretable forecasting.
- [Time Series Forecasting (5): Transformer Architecture for Time Series](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/transformer/): Transformers for time series, end to end: encoder-decoder anatomy, temporal positional encoding, the O(n^2) attention bottleneck, decoder-only forecasting, and patching. With variants (Autoformer, FEDformer, Informer, PatchTST) and a real implementation.
- [Time Series Forecasting (6): Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN)](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/temporal-convolutional-networks/): TCNs use causal dilated convolutions for parallel training and exponential receptive fields. Complete PyTorch implementation with traffic flow and sensor data case studies.
- [Time Series Forecasting (7): N-BEATS — Interpretable Deep Architecture](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/n-beats/): N-BEATS combines deep learning expressiveness with classical decomposition interpretability. Basis function expansion, double residual stacking, and M4 competition analysis with full PyTorch code.
- [Time Series Forecasting (8): Informer — Efficient Long-Sequence Forecasting](https://www.chenk.top/en/time-series/informer-long-sequence/): Informer reduces Transformer complexity from O(L^2) to O(L log L) via ProbSparse attention, distilling, and a one-shot generative decoder. Full math, PyTorch code, and ETT/weather benchmarks.

## Transfer Learning

- [Transfer Learning (1): Fundamentals and Core Concepts](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/01-fundamentals-and-core-concepts/): A beginner-friendly guide to transfer learning fundamentals: why it works, formal definitions, taxonomy, negative transfer, and a complete feature-transfer implementation with MMD domain adaptation.
- [Transfer Learning (2): Pre-training and Fine-tuning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/02-pre-training-and-fine-tuning/): Why pre-training learns a powerful prior from unlabeled data and how fine-tuning adapts it to your task. Covers contrastive learning, masked language models, discriminative learning rates, layer freezing, catastrophic forgetting, LoRA, and a production-ready BERT fine-tuning implementation.
- [Transfer Learning (3): Domain Adaptation](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/03-domain-adaptation/): A practical guide to domain adaptation: covariate shift, label shift, DANN with gradient reversal, MMD alignment, CORAL, self-training, AdaBN, and a complete DANN implementation.
- [Transfer Learning (4): Few-Shot Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/04-few-shot-learning/): Learn new concepts from a handful of examples. Covers the N-way K-shot protocol, metric learning (Siamese, Prototypical, Matching, Relation networks), meta-learning (MAML, Reptile), episodic training, miniImageNet benchmarks, and a complete Prototypical Network implementation.
- [Transfer Learning (5): Knowledge Distillation](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/05-knowledge-distillation/): Compress large teacher models into small student models without losing much accuracy. Covers dark knowledge, temperature scaling, response-based / feature-based / relation-based distillation, self-distillation, and a complete multi-strategy implementation.
- [Transfer Learning (6): Multi-Task Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/06-multi-task-learning/): Train one model on multiple tasks simultaneously. Covers hard vs. soft parameter sharing, gradient conflicts (PCGrad, GradNorm, CAGrad), auxiliary task design, and a complete multi-task framework with dynamic weight balancing.
- [Transfer Learning (7): Zero-Shot Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/07-zero-shot-learning/): A first-principles tour of zero-shot learning: attribute prototypes (DAP), compatibility functions, DeViSE, generative ZSL with f-CLSWGAN, the GZSL bias problem and calibration, and CLIP-style vision-language pretraining, with PyTorch building blocks.
- [Transfer Learning (8): Multimodal Transfer](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/08-multimodal-transfer/): Derive contrastive learning (InfoNCE), CLIP's vision-language pretraining, BLIP's Q-Former bridge to LLMs, cross-modal alignment, and multimodal fusion strategies. Includes a from-scratch CLIP implementation in PyTorch.
- [Transfer Learning (9): Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/09-parameter-efficient-fine-tuning/): Derive LoRA's low-rank adaptation, the Adapter bottleneck, Prefix-Tuning, Prompt-Tuning, BitFit and QLoRA. Includes a from-scratch LoRA implementation with weight merging and a method-selection guide.
- [Transfer Learning (10): Continual Learning](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/10-continual-learning/): Derive catastrophic forgetting from gradient interference and the Fisher information matrix. Covers EWC, MAS, LwF, replay (ER/A-GEM), dynamic architectures, the three CL scenarios, FWT/BWT metrics, and a from-scratch EWC implementation.
- [Transfer Learning (11): Cross-Lingual Transfer](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/11-cross-lingual-transfer/): Derive cross-lingual transfer from bilingual word-embedding alignment to multilingual pretraining (mBERT, XLM-R). Covers zero-shot transfer, translate-train vs translate-test, pivot strategies, subword anchors, the high/low-resource gap, and cross-lingual prompts.
- [Transfer Learning (12): Industrial Applications and Best Practices](https://www.chenk.top/en/transfer-learning/12-industrial-applications-and-best-practices/): Series finale. A field guide to shipping transfer learning to production: when to use it, the end-to-end pipeline, compute and dollar economics, four landmark case studies, A/B testing, distribution-shift monitoring, and 12-month ROI.

## Standalone

- [Graph Neural Networks for Learning Equivariant Representations of Neural Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/gnn-equivariant-representations/): Represent a neural network as a directed graph (neurons as nodes, weights as edges) and use a GNN to produce permutation-equivariant embeddings. The right symmetry unlocks generalisation prediction, network classification, retrieval, and model merging across architectures and widths.
- [Operating System Fundamentals: A Deep Dive](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/operating-system-fundamentals-deep-dive/): Walk through processes, virtual memory, file systems, the I/O stack, system calls and schedulers, with the actual numbers and the commands you can verify each claim with on a Linux box.
- [Multimodal LLMs and Downstream Tasks: A Practitioner's Guide](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/multimodal-llm-downstream-tasks/): End-to-end map of multimodal LLMs: vision-language alignment, cross-modal fusion, the CLIP/BLIP/LLaVA families, downstream tasks (VQA, captioning, grounding, OCR), fine-tuning trade-offs, benchmarks, and what it takes to ship one in production.
- [LLMGR: Integrating Large Language Models with Graphical Session-Based Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/llmgr/): LLMGR uses an LLM as the semantic engine for session-based recommendation and a GNN as the ranker. Covers the hybrid encoding layer, two-stage prompt tuning, ~8.68% HR@20 lift, and how to deploy without running an LLM per request.
- [Graph Contextualized Self-Attention Network (GC-SAN) for Session-based Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/gcsan/): GC-SAN combines a session-graph GGNN (local transitions) with multi-layer self-attention (global dependencies) for session-based recommendation. Covers graph construction, message passing, attention fusion, and where the design wins or breaks.
- [Session-based Recommendation with Graph Neural Networks (SR-GNN)](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/session-based-recommendation-with-graph-neural-networks/): SR-GNN turns a click session into a directed weighted graph and runs a gated GNN to predict the next item. Covers session-graph construction, GGNN updates, attention-based session pooling, training, benchmarks, and the failure modes that decide whether you should reach for it.
- [paper2repo: GitHub Repository Recommendation for Academic Papers](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/paper2repo-github-repository-recommendation/): paper2repo aligns academic papers with GitHub repositories in a shared embedding space using a constrained GCN. Covers the joint heterogeneous graph, the WARP ranking loss, the cosine alignment constraint, and the full inference path.
- [Variational Autoencoder (VAE): From Intuition to Implementation and Troubleshooting](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/vae-guide/): Build a VAE from scratch in PyTorch. Covers the ELBO objective, reparameterization trick, posterior collapse fixes, beta-VAE, and a complete training pipeline.
- [LAMP Stack on Alibaba Cloud ECS: From Fresh Instance to Production-Ready Web Server](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/lamp-on-ecs/): Set up a LAMP stack (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP) on Alibaba Cloud ECS. Covers security groups, service installation, Discuz deployment, source compilation, hardening and three-tier scale-out.
- [Position Encoding Brief: From Sinusoidal to RoPE and ALiBi](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/position-encoding-brief/): A practitioner's tour of Transformer position encoding: why attention needs it at all, how sinusoidal/learned/relative/RoPE/ALiBi schemes differ, and which one to pick when long-context extrapolation matters.
- [HCGR: Hyperbolic Contrastive Graph Representation Learning for Session-based Recommendation](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/hcgr/): HCGR embeds session graphs in the Lorentz model of hyperbolic space and trains them with InfoNCE-style contrastive learning. This review unpacks why hierarchical session intent fits hyperbolic geometry, how Lorentz attention works in tangent space, and what the ablations actually prove.
- [Tennis-Scene Computer Vision: From Paper Survey to Production](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/tennis-cv-system-design/): A complete CV system for tennis: small high-speed object detection, multi-camera 3D reconstruction, physics-based trajectory prediction, and pose-based action recognition. From the literature down to a 16.7 ms-per-frame deployment budget.
- [MoSLoRA: Mixture-of-Subspaces in Low-Rank Adaptation](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/moslora/): MoSLoRA boosts LoRA expressivity by mixing multiple low-rank subspaces with a lightweight mixer. Covers when vanilla LoRA fails, mixer design choices, and tuning tips.
- [Low-Rank Matrix Approximation and the Pseudoinverse: From SVD to Regularization](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/low-rank-approximation-pseudoinverse/): From the least-squares view to the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, the four Penrose conditions, computation via SVD, truncated SVD, Tikhonov regularization, and modern applications from PCA to LoRA.
- [Symplectic Geometry and Structure-Preserving Neural Networks](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/symplectic-geometry-and-structure-preserving-neural-networks/): Learn physics-informed neural networks that preserve energy and symplectic structure. Covers HNN, LNN, SympNet, symplectic integrators, and four classical experiments.
- [Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/prefix-tuning/): Prefix-Tuning adapts frozen LLMs by learning continuous key/value vectors injected into attention. Covers the method, reparameterization, KV-cache mechanics, and comparisons with prompt tuning, adapters, and LoRA.
- [Reparameterization Trick & Gumbel-Softmax: A Deep Dive](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/reparameterization-gumbel-softmax/): Make sense of the reparameterization trick and Gumbel-Softmax: why gradients can flow through sampling, how temperature trades bias for variance, and the practical pitfalls of training discrete latent variables end-to-end.
- [LLM Workflows and Application Architecture: Enterprise Implementation Guide](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/llm-workflows-architecture/): From a single API call to a production LLM platform — workflow patterns, RAG, model routing, deployment, cost levers, observability, and enterprise integration, with the trade-offs that actually matter.
- [Prompt Engineering Complete Guide: From Zero to Advanced Optimization](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/prompt-engineering-complete-guide/): Master prompt engineering from zero-shot basics to Tree of Thoughts, DSPy, and automated optimization. Includes benchmarks, code, and a debugging toolkit.
- [AI Agents Complete Guide: From Theory to Industrial Practice](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/ai-agents-complete-guide/): A practitioner-grade guide to building AI agents: planning (CoT/ReAct/ToT), memory architectures, tool use, reflection, multi-agent patterns, frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI), evaluation, and production concerns.
- [When Every Trader Uses the Same AI: A Simulation of Market Fragility](https://www.chenk.top/en/standalone/ai-signal-market-fragility/): If a crowd of AI traders reads the same public data through similar models, their decisions converge — and that convergence can become a systemic stampede. A synthetic + LLM-agent simulation of when private rationality turns into shared fragility, and one hedge that measurably helps.
